title: Maths Knowledge Graph options
description: Reference schema for the maths-knowledge-graph configuration mapping. It is supplied for explicit external validation; the extension does not register automatic Quarto editor integration. The native filter remains authoritative for effective rebased paths and its UTF-8 byte bounds.

enabled.description: Enable mathematical catalogue validation, finite templates and optional notation. False leaves native source unchanged without reading catalogue or registry files.

import-accessible-maths.description: Automatically consume a compatible separately installed current-AST Accessible Maths catalogue only when that producer's catalogue option and per-declaration reviewed/public/scope policy opt in. False disables import. Missing/disabled/incompatible producers retain an unavailable/disabled result, not guessed data. Install and select both filters for AM rendering; installation alone does not activate it. Import-only pages require no empty knowledge.yml.

graph.description: When an existing KG composition run is prepared, project selected explicitly public native-visible mathematics into its separate maths graph. Existing author-declared and AM author-reviewed qualifications remain separate. No website canonical catalogue is rewritten. Use one empty page-level .maths-graph Div with placement: placeholder; false disables the bridge. Native mathematical reading remains available without KG/HTML.

declarations.description: Optional authoritative local literal YAML or JSON catalogue. If absent, reuse knowledge-graph.declarations; otherwise discover knowledge.yml, knowledge.yaml, then knowledge.json at the project/document root. Explicit paths follow Quarto's effective metadata rebasing.

notation.description: Optional local literal YAML or JSON notation registry, using notation.schema.json. Absence disables notation authoring; it does not request a network resource or a model.

notation-defaults.description: Page author defaults, below validated reader preferences and above registry defaults.

notation-overrides.description: Required page choices for compatible declared profiles. These take precedence over reader choices without erasing them.

notation-preferences.description: Explicit local exported notation JSON for native AST/Word/PDF output. Maximum 64 KiB, depth 8, exact current registry identity. It never enables browser persistence.

kernel-host.description: Optional explicitly configured HTTPS HTML host page (or HTTP loopback) at the same origin as a separately installed pinned Sandbox runtime. No kernel or model is downloaded during rendering.

formal-proofs.description: Opt-in deterministic constructive controlled-English proof candidates, including scoped subproofs/cases and explicitly reviewed public prose-proposal imports. Rendering never calls a model or accepts a private raw response. Source fidelity and optional kernel checking remain separate; quantifiers/equality/general mathematical prose remain unsupported by the finite compiler.

reuse-relations.description: Explicit qualified relation reuse on this page. Exact public identity, matching declared assertion revision/assumption digest and both current endpoint occurrences are required. No automatic semantic-equivalence or transitive-relation claim.

scopes.description: Optional exact mathematical scope names selected from a shared mixed catalogue. Selected objects and relations retain every normal publication/type/source validation; selected relations must resolve entirely within selected scopes. This is a view boundary, not a privacy or extraction boundary.

localDataPath.description: Relative local path with no controls, URI scheme, query or fragment. Forward/backslash separators are admitted in effective metadata. Dot components must resolve within the project/document root; the installed reader verifies canonical descendants and refuses symlink/junction aliases. This is a file-read boundary, not an operating-system sandbox or hostile concurrent-writer guarantee. The native 4096 limit is UTF-8 bytes; JSON Schema maxLength counts Unicode code points. No filename extension is inferred or enforced.
